blocks.text: CEBU CITY — Cebu’s recurring air pollution episodes and limited air quality monitoring capacity have made the province a key focus of a new campaign for cleaner air. The campaign was conceived amid the province’s growing air quality concerns, particularly pollution from industrial facilities, vehicle emissions and episodes of transboundary haze, organizers from Clean Air Asia said. Nearly 900 megawatts of coal-fired power generation capacity in Toledo City and Naga City, coupled with intensive traffic emissions in urban areas, contribute to the province’s air pollution, said the newly launched Cebu Clean Air Network (Cebu CAN).
